display.title: Episode 543: Reb Asher the Melamed, Chapter 3 (Elul)
display.summary_short: Elul is the wake-up month for teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah; in the final chapter, the minister turns out to be the orphan Reb Asher raised, and the decree is torn up.
display.summary_long: Broadcast early in Elul 5752. Uncle Yossi explains that Elul, the last month of the year, is the time to improve our midos, say brachos and daven slowly and carefully, give more tzedakah and do teshuvah. The shofar blown in shul every weekday morning of Elul is like an alarm clock, as the Rambam explains, waking us to teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah before the new year. After the march, a recap and the Shema led by a fifth-grade girl, story time brings the final chapter of 'Reb Asher the Melamed'. Thirty years earlier, a fire killed a family, leaving one non-Jewish child alone. Reb Asher took him in, fed and clothed him and brought him to cheder, until a relative came for him. That boy grew up to be the minister. He remembered Reb Asher teaching that nothing is greater than mesiras nefesh al kiddush Hashem, and even sings the tune Reb Asher used, so he arranged the test as a 'priceless gift'. Then he tears up the decree, and Reb Asher explains that the Baal Shem Tov knew whom to send. The show ends with Tehillim for the Rebbe's recovery and candle-lighting time.
display.lesson: Kindness comes back in unexpected ways; trust Hashem and the tzaddik, and be ready to stand firm for Hashem's honor.

date.note: 'Here we are in the month of Elul' (Rosh Chodesh Elul was 29-30 August 1992); Friday candle-lighting 7:05 matches 4 September 1992; the week of 25 August seems to have no new episode.
